sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Checking tools and installing packages
sections.what: Checks that Python and Node are present, creates a virtual environment in backend, installs backend packages, copies the example settings file if needed, then installs frontend packages.
sections.why: Gets a new computer ready in one step.
sections.watch_out: Backend package installation fails on Linux and macOS because of the Windows-only Outlook package.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Creating data folders and printing next steps
sections.what: Creates the data, log and results folders and prints how to add credentials and start the backend and frontend.
sections.why: Folders must exist before the app writes into them.
sections.watch_out: The printed version requirements are not enforced by the checks above.

summary: A first-time setup script that checks tools, installs backend and frontend packages, and creates the data folders.
purpose: Prepares a new computer so the app can be run.
why: Likely reason: one command replaces many manual setup steps.
how: Checks that Python and Node are present, creates a virtual environment in backend, installs backend packages, copies the example settings file if none exists, installs frontend packages, copies the frontend example settings, creates the data and log folders, and prints the next steps.
inputs: The requirements file, the example settings files, and the installed Python and Node tools.
outputs: A virtual environment, installed packages, settings files, empty data and log folders, and printed instructions.
risks: The backend install fails on Linux and macOS because of the Windows-only Outlook package. The version checks only confirm that Python and Node exist, so the stated minimum versions are not enforced. Settings files contain credentials, so the copied file needs care.
debug: If pip install fails, look for the pywin32 line. If a tool is reported missing, install it and run the script again. If settings are wrong, edit backend/.env and frontend/.env.local.
